Concentrated finding round (unified triage seat, 2026-08-17): **promoted to `pm:queue`**, type `Bug`. Wrong-mechanism defect with a measured repro chain: the sessionStorage seed is keyed by metadata type only, so after an org switch every `useMetadata().apps` consumer in the seed window reads the previous org's data, and a cached `[]` is truthy so it also suppresses `initialLoading`. The visible strand was patched downstream (PR #4483's bounce) but the provider still serves cross-org data. Scope = the card's one keying decision: include the active org identifier in the storage key (or invalidate on org change) and treat cached-empty as a miss for `initialLoading`. Cross-org staleness has a privacy smell as well as a correctness one — say in the PR whether any cached fields are org-confidential. M / opus.

Serial constraints cleared: `providers/` is free; no open PR touches it. Region-disjoint from all three siblings this round.

**Parallelism disciplines (all four binding):** region declared above; merge `main` before opening the PR; merge again if a sibling lands first; conflicts go to the merge queue — ⛔ never resolve a sibling's hunks.

## Zone 1 — scope is one keying decision (triage, comment-5320928326)

Two defects, one mechanism:
1. **Cross-org staleness** — the sessionStorage seed (`objectui:metadata:app`) is keyed by metadata **type only**, so after an org switch every `useMetadata().apps` consumer in the seed window reads the **previous org's** app list.
2. **Truthy-empty short-circuit** — `loadFromSession` returning `[]` is truthy, so a cached empty list also suppresses `initialLoading`; "no apps (cached, possibly stale)" is indistinguishable from "no apps (fresh)".

The ruled scope: include the active org identifier in the storage key (or invalidate on org change), and treat a cached empty list as a **miss** for the `initialLoading` decision. Both are the same one keying decision.

## Zone 2 — the privacy question, carried verbatim from triage

> Cross-org staleness has a privacy smell as well as a correctness one — say in the PR whether any cached fields are org-confidential.

Answer that explicitly in the PR body. Enumerate what the cache actually holds and state whether any of it is org-scoped data that should never have been readable after a workspace switch. This is not a formality: if the answer is yes, that reframes the card's severity and I need to know before it lands, because it changes what has to be said in the changeset and possibly whether existing cached data needs invalidating on upgrade rather than merely re-keyed going forward.

**If it turns out org-confidential data is being served across a boundary, stop and report `needs_decision`** — that is a maintainer call, not a keying fix.

## Zone 3 — what makes this card easy to under-fix

The card is honest that PR #4483 already patched the **visible** strand (a bounce), so nothing user-facing is broken today. That makes it tempting to key the cache and stop. Two things resist that:

- The card's own point is that **any other consumer** of `useMetadata().apps` in the seed window inherits the same wrong answer — `RootLandingRedirect` was simply the one that got caught. Fixing the key without pinning the invariant leaves the next consumer exposed.
- The truthy-empty half is a **separate** failure mode and is easy to drop on the floor while doing the keying. Pin it separately.

Pin the invariant, not the symptom: after an org switch, a `useMetadata().apps` read in the seed window must not return the previous org's list. A test that only asserts the storage key string would pass against a re-keying that still serves stale data on some path.

**Out of scope, named so you do not wander:** #4522 (`AppContent`'s `missingRecheck` — different layer, different cache, currently in flight on a sibling claim) and PR #4483's bounce. The card names both as distinct.

## Gates

Derive from your diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the four test shards, changeset gates, `Control Byte Scan`. A clue, not a spec. Changeset required (`@object-ui/app-shell`).

## Premise-first

The card is from 2026-08-12 and re-verified by triage on 2026-08-17. Re-measure the seed path yourself before editing; if the provider has been restructured, follow what you measure — `premise_still_valid: false` with evidence is a legitimate delivery.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #4486`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report AND post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5199 (`repo:objectui` seat PM, session `session_01AMHbqfPiETJHA95r6WzZWS`, reviewer of record).

## Keying the storage alone would have passed a naive test and still served stale data

This is the part that makes the card, and you found it rather than being told:

> `console/organizations/manage/OrganizationLayout` calls `switchOrganization` from an effect with **no reload at all**, where the in-memory cache answers `useMetadata().apps` and would stay stale until the 5-minute TTL

So the storage key was never the whole mechanism. The ruled fix said "include the active org identifier in the storage key **or invalidate on org change**", and the honest reading turned out to be *both* — the provider now also drops the in-memory cache on an org change. A test asserting only the storage-key string would have gone green over a live defect, which is exactly the shape the dispatch warned about and exactly the shape your test avoids: every assertion reads what a consumer gets back, not what the key spells.

## The org identifier's source is a reasoned choice, not a convenient one

Reading it from `ActiveOrganizationStorage` because that is **the same value `createAuthenticatedFetch` stamps as `X-Tenant-ID` on the `/meta` request that fills the cache** makes the cache scope equal the tenant the server actually filtered for. That is the correct invariant to key on, and the rejection of the obvious alternative is equally well-reasoned: `useAuth().activeOrganization?.id` resolves asynchronously and would be `null` at seed time, missing every boot.

You also avoided a known regression rather than rediscovering it: treating the first `null → id` resolution as **not** a switch, because it happens on every boot and clearing there would refetch the eager types mid-flight — objectui#4042 — and pinning that with its own case.

## The privacy question, answered rather than deflected

Triage asked whether any cached fields are org-confidential. You enumerated the contents (app definitions per `AppSchema`: name, label, navigation tree, `requiredPermissions`, `contextSelectors.optionsSource.endpoint`, `_provenance`/`_lock*`/`_package*` — **no record rows, no field values, no user data, no credentials**), then reached a conclusion and defended it:

> on the org-switch path no principal gains anything it was not entitled to: sessionStorage is per-origin AND per-tab, and the reader is the same signed-in user switching within their own server-gated membership list — they were authorised to read org A's list seconds earlier

That is the right call and the right reason. Escalating on the word "privacy" without that analysis would have been theatre; not doing the analysis at all would have been negligence. You also drew the correct consequence for the upgrade question — re-keying going forward suffices — while still deleting the stale unscoped entry because it costs one line.

## And you found the case that ISN'T this one

**#5198** is the finding of the round: `signOut` clears only `TokenStorage` — neither the `objectui:metadata:*` entries nor `ActiveOrganizationStorage` — and no sign-out call site reloads, so **a different user signing into the same tab and the same org is still seeded from the previous user's permission-filtered app list**. Genuinely cross-principal, unlike this card, and — the part that makes it worth filing rather than folding in — **org-keying cannot close it**, because two users in one org produce the same key.

Filing that separately instead of widening this PR is correct on both counts: it is a different mechanism, and it is a different severity class. I am flagging it to the maintainer in my final report; grading it is the triage seat's, not mine.

## Verified against the tree

3 files (`MetadataProvider.tsx`, its new test, changeset). Branch contains current `main` (`57e668f13`). **OUT list clean** — nothing under `console/**`, `views/**`, `hooks/**` or `utils/**`, so all three sibling claims this round were respected. Reverse verification predicted red and observed 4 red / 2 green, with the two greens being deliberate counter-pins (same-org remount still seeds instantly, so the tests cannot be satisfied by simply deleting the cache; `null → id` does not clear, protecting the #4042 request budget). The ablation binds to source via the repo's vitest aliases — stated with its reason rather than assumed.

Worth noting for the record: you caught your own missing changeset by **reading the PR back** after opening it. That read-back is a discipline this repo needs more of, not less.

**Landing:** `packages/app-shell/src/providers/**` + changeset — no governed face, queue-eligible. Flipping ready and enqueuing on terminal success of every required job, read by name.
